params.body:
The screen opened on a fixed thirty days while the traces behind it reach back to 2020. That answered "is this week busy" and refused the question the screen was asked for first: is the platform busier than it was.

Four windows now: 30 days, 90 days, 12 months, or everything since 1 October 2020 — the same start Inzichten uses, because two screens should not disagree about when the platform began. The choice sits in the URL (`?periode=`), so a window worth talking about can be sent as a link rather than as "click the third tab".

## Per month above four months

Five years of days is eighteen hundred bars of about half a pixel each, and the eye reads noise where the chart promised a trend. Above 120 days the series is drawn per month, which turns those five years into sixty bars and makes the growth visible. The threshold sits above the 90-day window so that one still shows its days.

The count of active garages is the reason the grain sits in the query rather than in a fold in PHP: a garage that worked on twenty days is one garage, not twenty, so it cannot be added up after the fact.

## What follows the window and what does not

The window drives the series, the composition and the busiest garages. Two things stay where they are, and the rule says why: the rhythm per hour and per weekday keeps its ninety days, because one month cannot tell you anything about a Tuesday, and "quiet" keeps its thirty, because a garage that did nothing in five years is not an operational question.

Over the whole history there is no period before it, so the comparison is **absent** there rather than zero. A zero in that column reads as a collapse.

## What it shows now

The monthly series is the point of this change. It goes from a handful of garages in 2022 to around a hundred active every month since 2025, and September 2026 at 1,726 handlings is the second-busiest month on record.

It also answers the question that prompted this. Around the migration of 15 September:

```
01/09 - 14/09  (before)   876 handlings   63 per day
15/09 - 25/09  (after)    850 handlings   77 per day
15/08 - 25/08  (a month earlier, same 11 days)   517   47 per day
```

No dip. Worth saying plainly, though: this measures what dealers *did*, not how much was *looked at*, and eleven days is a short window.

## Verified

Three tests added: that a long window is drawn per month and a short one per day with the right number of steps and well-formed labels, that an unknown window from the URL falls back to the default instead of emptying the page, and that the whole history carries no comparison while a normal window does.

New rule R P3-16.7. Full suite: 2,177 tests, with only the two known `ListPageHeadersTest` cases failing, which fail the same way without this change because those tables are empty in my local database. `phpstan` green, `pint` green.
params.title: Activity over longer windows
